dedupe_keys.name: construction and demolition model to track material flows and embodied carbon gothenburg residential stock

description: This model is a spatially explicit, rule-based simulation of the material stock in a city's buildings, built to see how reuse of existing materials could cut the footprint of construction and demolition. It follows construction, demolition and renovation over space and time and tests the effects of reusing recycled materials, demolitions, renovations and building typologies on material flows and embodied carbon, using factors for product stages A1 to A3. The case study is the residential building stock of Gothenburg with eight building materials tracked, a baseline scenario and a hypothetical policy scenario. It was published by Jonathan Edgardo Cohen on CoMSES in September 2024 for the GAMA platform. Coverage: Gothenburg, Sweden. Access: free code on CoMSES. Licence: Apache-2.0. Caveats: a proof of concept; not peer reviewed on CoMSES. Simulation uses are circular economy and embodied carbon scenarios for urban building stocks and planning of demolition and reuse. Related records: ODYM-based building stock models such as the Swiss residential building stock model.
